question.problem: The inverse of the function $f(x)=5{log}_{4}⁡(10x-1)$ is ${f}^{-1}(x)=${{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
To find ${f}^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =5{log}_{4}⁡(10x-1)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =5{log}_{4}⁡(10y-1).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =5{log}_{4}⁡(10y-1) \\ {log}_{4}⁡(10y-1) & =\frac{x}{5} \\ {4}^{{log}_{4}⁡(10y-1)} & ={4}^{x/5} \\ 10y-1 & ={4}^{x/5} \\ 10y & ={4}^{x/5}+1 \\ y & =\frac{{4}^{x/5}+1}{10}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse function is ${f}^{-1}(x)=\frac{{4}^{x/5}+1}{10}.$
